discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms for quantum simulation and quantum information processing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Over two decades, the nominees turned the Rydberg blockade from a theoretical proposal into a platform that controls hundreds of neutral atoms one at a time. Saffman and Browaeys made the first observations of the blockade between two individual atoms held in optical tweezers, and Saffman showed the first neutral-atom entangling gates. Lukin co-proposed blockade-based quantum gates. Browaeys and Lukin then built reconfigurable, defect-free tweezer arrays, which they used to realise programmable quantum simulators of Ising-type spin models. These revealed quantum phase transitions, many-body scars and topological spin liquids. The Lukin group recently demonstrated logical qubits with error detection and correction. Together this work gives a new, microscopic window on strongly correlated quantum matter. It has become one of the leading routes to scalable quantum computation. It is a textbook case of careful experimental atomic physics growing into a new field and a new technology.
